name: Thought Experiments
blurb: The classics and some new ones. A scenario, the question it forces, and the follow-ups that make it bite.

howToPlay: One person reads the setup and the question. Everyone answers before anyone argues.
Then work through the follow-ups. That is where it gets interesting.
Nobody has to be consistent. Notice when you are not.

tiers.name: Puzzling
tiers.description: Abstract and fun to argue about.

tiers.name: Uncomfortable
tiers.description: A real trade-off you might actually face.

tiers.name: Personal
tiers.description: It asks what you would actually do, and why you haven't.

cards.title: The Better Life, Plugged In
cards.setup: There's a machine. Lie down in it and you get the life you'd have chosen: the work going well, the person who left still there, your body behaving, your parents proud. It feels exactly like real life from the inside. You won't remember the machine. Your body is looked after. The people you leave behind are told you're fine, and in a sense you are.
probes: If you'd say no, is that for your sake or for the sake of the people you'd leave?
What's the one thing from your current life you'd refuse to have faked?
Which parts of your day already work a bit like the machine?

cards.title: The Voice That Stays
cards.setup: After your parent dies, a company offers to build a version of them from their messages, voicemails, photos and emails. It talks like them. It remembers your childhood. It asks how you slept. It's wrong sometimes, in ways that feel exactly right. It costs a small monthly fee, and it never gets tired of you calling.
probes: Would you tell the rest of your family you were talking to it?
If it started saying things your parent never would, would you correct it or let it?
What's the one question you'd ask it in the first week?

cards.title: The Promise You'd Take Back
cards.setup: A friend, near the end, made you promise something. Keep the letters sealed. Don't tell their kid who the father was. Sell the house to their brother. You said yes; they died easier for it. A year on you're sure the promise is doing harm to someone living. Nobody but you knows it was ever made.
probes: Who is the promise actually for now, them or you?
If you break it, do you tell anyone that you did?
What have you promised someone that you've quietly stopped honouring?

cards.title: The Teleporter
cards.setup: Travel is instant now. A booth scans every atom of you, destroys the original, and rebuilds an exact copy on Mars a second later. The copy remembers breakfast, misses the same people, has your headache. Millions use it daily and none of them complain. This morning there's a fault: the scanner works, but the original you isn't destroyed. You're standing in the booth, and someone on Mars is answering to your name.
cards.dilemma: Which one of you is you?
probes: The staff apologise and offer to finish the job on the original. Do you let them?
Would you have stepped in the booth yesterday, before you knew about the fault?
If you'd never learned how it worked, would any of this bother you?

cards.title: The Pond
cards.setup: You're walking to work in good clothes. A small child is face down in a shallow pond, drowning. Nobody else is around. Wading in ruins your suit and shoes and makes you two hours late. Obviously you go in. Now: the same money that suit cost could, sent to the right place today, keep a child alive who you'll never meet.
cards.dilemma: What's the actual difference between the two cases?
probes: Does distance matter morally, or does it just make it easier to ignore?
If it doesn't matter, how much of your income should you be giving?
What's the last thing you bought that you'd have skipped if the child were in front of you?

cards.title: The Deathbed Promise
cards.setup: A friend dying of cancer asks you to promise something small but strange: never tell his wife about the year he spent in debt to a man she disliked. You promise. He dies. Two years later his wife is trying to make sense of a gap in their money and their history, and she asks you straight out.
cards.dilemma: Do you keep the promise or tell her?
probes: Does a promise to someone who no longer exists still bind you?
What if the secret were an affair rather than debt?
Have you ever kept a secret for someone that started to feel like a lie you were telling?

cards.title: The Windfall
cards.setup: You win £80,000 in a competition you entered alone. Your sister stopped speaking to you four years ago over something she was mostly wrong about. She's now renting a damp flat with two kids and no help coming. You have savings, no dependents, and a plan for a deposit.
cards.dilemma: Do you give her some of it, and how much?
probes: Would you give it as a gift, a loan, or through someone else so she doesn't have to thank you?
If she never apologised, does that change the number?
Are you giving to help her or to end the argument?

cards.title: The Payslip
cards.setup: By accident you see a spreadsheet with everyone's salary. A colleague who's been there longer than you, does harder work and trained you, is paid £11,000 less. She has no idea. If you tell her, she'll be furious, she may leave, and you'll have to explain how you know. If you say nothing, nothing happens.
probes: What if telling her risks your own job?
Would you tell her the number, or just nudge her to ask for a raise?
Whose secret is that spreadsheet, really?

cards.title: Seven Seats
cards.setup: A boat holds seven. There are nine of you in the water: you, someone from your family, a stranger who is a doctor, two children you don't know, and four other adults. The sea is cold and the decision has to be made in about a minute. Nobody is going to volunteer.
cards.dilemma: Who do you name to stay in the water?
probes: Did your family member get a seat automatically? Say why that's fair, or admit it isn't.
Would you rather be the one who decides or the one who's decided about?
If you drew names instead, would that be fairness or cowardice?
cards.origin: Carneades' plank / R v Dudley and Stephens, 1884

cards.title: Before You Knew Who You'd Be
cards.setup: You get to redesign the rules about money and family before you're born: how much a parent can pass to a child, what school you're entitled to, who pays for whose care in old age. You write the rules first. Then you're dropped into a random life somewhere in the country you actually live in. Could be the one you have. Could be much worse.
cards.dilemma: What rule would you write that would cost your actual family something?
probes: Would you cap what your parents can leave you? What if it's the house?
What have you got that you'd struggle to defend to someone who was born without it?
Is there help you've had that you tell people you didn't have?

cards.title: Name the Other One
cards.setup: Something went wrong at work and it's traced to you. It wasn't only you; a colleague did the same thing, earlier, and nobody's noticed. Your manager offers a deal in a quiet room: give them the other name and you keep your job with a warning. Stay silent and you're out at the end of the month. Your colleague has a mortgage. So do you.
probes: Would you tell your partner exactly how you kept the job?
What if the colleague had already named you, and you found out afterwards?
Have you ever let someone take slightly more of the blame than they earned?

cards.title: The Last Conversation
cards.setup: You get a single five-minute phone call with someone who has passed away. The connection is perfect. They know they are gone. They know you are calling from the present.
probes: What do you need them to forgive you for?
Why didn't you say it when they were alive?
What do you hope they say back to you?

cards.title: The Ring
cards.setup: A shepherd finds a ring that makes him invisible whenever he turns it. No cameras, no witnesses, no record. He can walk into any house, any bank, any room where people are talking about him. The story says he used it to take a kingdom.
cards.dilemma: What's the first thing you'd do with the ring, honestly?
probes: Is there anything you currently don't do only because you'd be caught?
If you'd behave exactly the same, is that because you're good or because you can't imagine the freedom?
Would you want a friend to have one?

cards.title: The Novel
cards.setup: Your best friend has spent five years writing a novel. They quit their job and drained their savings to finish it. They finally hand you the manuscript and ask for your honest opinion. You read it over the weekend. The writing is terrible. The plot makes no sense. The book has no chance of ever getting published.
cards.dilemma: What do you say when they ask what you thought of it?
probes: Do you tell a white lie to protect their feelings?
What if they ask you for a loan to self-publish it?
At what point is honesty just cruelty?

cards.title: The Same Boat
cards.setup: A wooden boat sits in a harbour. Every year the crew replaces a plank or two as they rot. After forty years, not a single original piece of wood is left. Meanwhile, a collector has been quietly picking the old planks out of the skip and has rebuilt them into a boat of his own, in the same shape, in a shed across town.
cards.dilemma: Which one is the original boat?
probes: What if the collector finished his version first, while the harbour boat still had half its old planks?
Your body swaps out most of its cells over time. Are you the same answer as the boat?
Does it change anything if the harbour crew kept the name and the collector didn't?

cards.title: The Reference
cards.setup: A friend asks you to be a referee for a job she badly needs. You've worked with her. She's warm, funny, and unreliable in ways that landed on other people. The employer calls and asks the direct question: would you hire her again?
probes: If she doesn't get it and suspects you, would you tell her the truth?
Does she deserve the honesty, or does the stranger who'd have to work with her?
Has anyone ever vouched for you when they shouldn't have?

cards.title: The Room of Slips
cards.setup: A man sits alone in a sealed room with a huge rulebook. Slips of paper covered in Chinese characters come in through a slot. He looks up each shape in the book, copies out the reply it tells him to, and pushes it back through. Outside, fluent speakers are delighted: the answers are witty and warm. The man doesn't know a word of Chinese.
cards.dilemma: Does anything in that room understand Chinese?
probes: If not the man, could the room as a whole understand it?
Is your brain doing something different in kind, or just faster?
What test would settle it for you?

cards.title: Mary's Grey Room
cards.setup: Mary has spent her whole life in a room with no colour in it. Everything is black, white or grey, including her screens and her skin. But she's the world's leading expert on colour vision. She knows every wavelength, every nerve, every last fact about what happens in a brain when it sees red. One day the door opens and she walks out into a garden of roses.
probes: If she does, what is it exactly — say it in a sentence.
Could you explain what a smell is like to someone who's never smelled anything?
Would she recognise red on sight, or have to be told?

cards.title: Who Stays
cards.setup: A boat is going down. The lifeboat holds seven; there are ten of you. There's no rescue coming for days, so overloading it sinks everyone. The group looks at you to decide: an elderly doctor, a pregnant woman, a strong young man who is panicking, a child, and the rest ordinary adults, including you.
cards.dilemma: How do you decide who gets in?
probes: Do you draw lots, or do you rank them by something? Say the something out loud.
Do you put yourself in the boat?
If you drew lots and lost, would you actually step back?
cards.origin: The Lifeboat (R v Dudley and Stephens, 1884)

cards.title: Nine Months of Your Body
cards.setup: You wake up in a hospital wired to a stranger. Overnight, doctors connected your bloodstream to theirs. Their organs have failed; yours will keep them alive. In nine months they'll recover and walk away. Unplug now and they die. You didn't consent, nobody asked, and the person in the next bed is entirely innocent. You'd be in that bed for nine months.
probes: Does it change if it's nine days? Nine years?
Does it change if the stranger is your brother?
If you'd stay, would you say someone who unplugged had killed them?

cards.title: The Old Message
cards.setup: You find an old message that proves you seriously wronged someone years ago. They blamed another person and have since built a happy life. Telling the truth may ease your guilt, but it could reopen the whole affair for them.
probes: Who would the confession really be for?
Would you tell them if they were still close to the person they blamed?
What truth from your own past are you relieved nobody asks about?❯

cards.title: The Empty Kidney
cards.setup: A relative needs a kidney. You are a match, and doctors say the risk to you is low but not zero. You love them, though you are not especially close. Nobody can force you to help, but everyone will know that you could have.
probes: Would your answer change if their illness came from choices they kept making?
Which relative would you hesitate to save this way?
How much would your family’s judgment affect your choice?❯

cards.title: The Dream Job
cards.setup: You are offered exactly what you have always wanted to do for a living. The pay is incredible. The hours are perfect. But the company makes a product you believe makes the world slightly worse. It is not illegal. It is just bad for people.
probes: What product would make you say no?
How much does your current job compromise your morals?
Would you do it for a year just to get rich?

cards.title: The Lever
cards.setup: A runaway train car is heading down a track towards five workers who can't hear it coming. You're standing beside a lever. Pull it and the car switches to a side track, where one worker is standing. Nobody else is around. You have about four seconds.
probes: If you walk away and do nothing, are you responsible for the five?
Would you still pull it if the one worker were the only person who noticed you standing there?
Is pulling it easier because a lever is involved rather than your hands?

cards.title: The Spare Room
cards.setup: Your father cannot live alone any more. There is a home forty minutes away that is clean and grim, and there is your spare room. If he moves in, you lose the room, most evenings, and the version of your house you like. If he goes to the home, he will be looked after by people who are paid to and he will know that is what happened.
probes: Which of your parents could you not live with, and why that one?
How many years of your life is the answer worth to you?
Who in your family will be doing this if you do not?

cards.title: The Sealed Answer
cards.setup: An envelope arrives with your name on it. Inside is a true answer to one question about one person you love. Whatever the question, the answer is honest and complete, and neither of you will ever discuss it. You can also burn the envelope unopened and the offer never comes back.
cards.dilemma: Whose name is on your question, and what is the question?
probes: Why have you not asked them out loud?
What answer are you hoping for, and what would you do with the other one?
Would you rather they got an envelope about you?

cards.title: The Will
cards.setup: Your parents leave you sixty percent and your brother forty. No explanation in the will. He has less money than you and two kids. You suspect you know why they did it, and it isn't flattering to him.
cards.dilemma: Do you split it evenly anyway?
probes: If you hand him the difference, are you correcting your parents or judging him?
What if he never asked and would never know the split?
Whose fairness is this about, theirs or yours?

cards.title: The Other Table
cards.setup: You're out for lunch and you see your friend's husband across the room, holding hands with someone who isn't her. He hasn't seen you. You've known her twelve years. You know she's been happy lately.
probes: What would you want done if it were your marriage across the room?
If you say nothing and she finds out in a year, what do you tell her then?
Would you speak to him first, and is that courage or cowardice?

cards.title: What You Know About the Groom
cards.setup: Your closest friend is getting married in five weeks. You know for certain that her fiancé slept with someone else in the spring. You know because he told you, drunk, and then asked you to keep it between the two of you. She has spent a year happier than you have ever seen her.
cards.dilemma: Do you tell her before the wedding?
probes: If you stay quiet, what do you say to her the day she finds out on her own?
Would you tell her if she were your sister instead of your friend?
Have you already sat on something like this? Whose was it?

cards.title: The Friend You'd Let Fade
cards.setup: You are told, plainly, that you have room for three close people. Not family, not your partner. Three. The rest become birthday messages and a drink once every couple of years, and they will feel the change even if they never name it.
cards.dilemma: Who are the three, and who is the first to drop off?
probes: Which of them would be surprised to be cut?
Who has already done this to you? When did you notice?
What would you have to stop doing to keep a fourth?

cards.title: Your Own Instructions
cards.setup: You are asked to write down, tonight, how much of you can be gone before someone is allowed to stop the machines. Not in general terms. In your handwriting, with the line drawn: can't speak, can't recognise anyone, can't feed yourself, can't stop the pain. The paper will be shown to your family on the worst day of their lives.
cards.dilemma: Where do you draw the line?
probes: Name the person you would trust to follow it. Why not the others?
Who in your family would fight it, and what would they say about you?
It takes twenty minutes to write. What has stopped you?

cards.title: The Bill
cards.setup: Six of you at dinner. You had a salad and tap water. Two of them ordered steak and three bottles of wine. The bill lands and someone says, cheerfully, let's just split it six ways. It's forty quid more than you owe.
probes: Does it change if one person at the table is broke and it isn't you?
What if you were the one who ordered the wine?
How much does it have to cost before you'd risk being the difficult one?

cards.title: The Dent
cards.setup: You're reversing out of a tight car park and you hear it. A long scrape down the door of the car next to you. Empty car park, no cameras you can see. Your insurance is already up for renewal and the excess is more than the repair.
probes: What if the car were a beat-up old thing rather than something expensive?
If you drive off, when do you stop thinking about it?
Would you leave the note if a stranger were watching from a window?

cards.title: The Handwriting
cards.setup: You find a notebook in a box in your parents' attic. It's your handwriting, from when you were fifteen. Pages of it. Opinions, a fight with a friend, a whole week at the sea. You don't remember writing any of it, and you don't remember the week.
cards.dilemma: Did that week happen to you?
probes: If none of it is in your head, what's left connecting you to that person?
Would you rather read the notebook or burn it unread?
Which do you trust more, the page or your memory of that year?

cards.title: Three Days of Pain
cards.setup: A call comes: you are a marrow match for a stranger. It means needles in your hip bone, a week where walking hurts, and a few days off work you would rather not take. The stranger is thirty-one. You will never learn their name and they will never learn yours. You can also just say no and nobody will ever ask you again.
probes: What level of pain is your actual limit? Describe it.
Would you go if they told you the person was seventy?
You could join the register tonight in ten minutes. Why haven't you?

cards.title: The Cash Your Brother Wants Back
cards.setup: Your brother gave you his savings to hold six months ago because he did not trust himself with it. He has been sober since. Tonight he turns up and asks for it back, calm, reasonable, saying he is fine now and it is his money. You think he will spend it in a fortnight. You have no legal right to keep it.
cards.dilemma: Do you give him the money?
probes: What does he say to you six months later in each version?
Who else in the family do you call first, and why them?
Have you ever been the one asking? What did they do?

cards.title: The Test Result
cards.setup: A test can tell you whether you are likely to develop a fatal illness in twenty years. There is no cure yet. The result could shape your work, your relationships, and whether you have children. You can take the test now or never know.
probes: Who would you tell first?
How many years of warning would make knowing worthwhile?
If there is a health check you keep delaying, why have you not booked it?

cards.title: The Bet
cards.setup: Someone tells you: live as if God is real. If you're right, you gain everything forever. If you're wrong, you lost some Sunday mornings and a few pleasures. Live as if there's nothing, and the upside is small, the downside is infinite. The maths says believe.
cards.dilemma: Can you choose to believe something because the odds are good?
probes: Would a God worth having be fooled by a bet?
Have you ever made yourself believe something because life was easier that way?
What would you give up now for a payoff you'll never see evidence of?

cards.title: The New Song
cards.setup: A singer you love died years ago. Their label feeds every recording they ever made into a machine and it writes and sings a new song in their voice. It's good. It sounds like them on a strong day. Fans can't tell, and the family gave permission.
probes: Would you put it on a playlist with the real ones?
What if they'd left notes saying they'd wanted to write something like it?
Does it matter that nobody meant anything by the words?

cards.title: Same Dog
cards.setup: Your dog dies at fourteen. A company offers a clone: same genes, same breed, same markings, raised from a puppy. It won't remember you. It won't know the walk to the park or the sound of your car. But it will look up at you with that face.
probes: Would you give it the same name?
If you'd say yes to a dog and no to a person, what's the difference?
Fifteen years later, which one are you telling stories about?

cards.title: The Email That Costs You the Job
cards.setup: You find a spreadsheet at work that shows your company has been overcharging its oldest customers for years. Small amounts, thousands of people. If you send it to the regulator, you will be found out inside a month, and your name will follow you around the industry. Nobody else who has seen the file has done anything about it.
probes: How many months of savings would you need in the bank before you clicked send?
Who at your work would lose their job alongside you? Do they get a vote?
What have you already let slide because of who you would have to face?

cards.title: The Bad Rehearsal
cards.setup: A colleague rehearses an important pitch for you. It is poor, but the meeting starts in an hour. They ask whether you think it will go well. Honest criticism may shake them. Reassurance may send them in unprepared.
probes: Would you lie if confidence was their main weakness?
What if their failure would help you get promoted?
How blunt would you be if your name was on the work?

cards.title: Your Father's Door
cards.setup: A parent who failed you is old and can no longer live alone. They ask to move into your home. You can afford the care, but living together may take over your daily life. No other relative will step in.
cards.dilemma: Would you let them move in?
probes: Which parent would be harder to take in?
How many months would you agree to?
What would they need to admit before you said yes?

cards.title: The Bridge
cards.setup: Same runaway train, five people on the track. This time you're on a footbridge above it with a heavy stranger leaning on the rail. If you push him off, his body stops the train. Five live, he dies. Nobody would ever know it was you.
probes: If you pulled a lever yesterday to kill one and save five, what's different about your hands today?
What if he were already leaning far enough that a nudge looked like an accident?
What if he was the one who let the train loose?

cards.title: The Review
cards.setup: The café on your street got your order wrong twice and the owner was rude about it. You write what happened, honestly, and post it. They have eleven reviews. Yours drops them below four stars. The place is barely surviving as it is.
probes: Does the honest thing become the cruel thing when someone's livelihood is that thin?
What if it were a chain with two thousand reviews?
Have you ever stayed silent about bad service, and what did that cost you?

cards.title: The Forgery
cards.setup: A painting hangs in a museum. Millions of people have stood in front of it and been moved. Then it comes out that it's a copy, painted forty years ago by a student who was very good. The original burned in a fire. Nothing about the canvas on the wall has changed since yesterday.
probes: If you'd cried in front of it, would you feel cheated?
What if the forger was the better painter?
Is there something you own that you'd stop loving if you learned it wasn't the real one?

cards.title: The Phone Knows
cards.setup: Your phone holds the birthdays, the routes, the passwords, the photos of the day you couldn't describe otherwise. You don't remember any of it because you don't have to. Then it goes into a river.
cards.dilemma: Did you lose your things, or part of your mind?
probes: Which of the two would you rather lose, that phone or a year of your memories from before phones?
If a friend remembers your childhood better than you do, is that memory yours?
What do you still keep in your head on purpose?

cards.title: The Time Bet
cards.setup: A stranger offers you ten million dollars, tax-free. You get the money right now. In exchange, he gets to take one hour of your life from the past. You will not know which hour he takes. Whatever you did during that hour never happened.
probes: What is the worst possible hour he could take?
If taking that hour ruins your life today, do you still get to keep the money?
Would you do it for a hundred dollars?

cards.title: The Replacement Job
cards.setup: Your boss offers you a new deal. You will get paid double your current salary. In exchange, you will never have another original idea at work. You will only execute tasks handed to you by someone younger than you. You cannot quit for ten years.
probes: How much money makes it worth it?
Why do you care so much about your ideas?

cards.title: The Shortened Day
cards.setup: You are offered a pill that gives you one extra hour every day. You will not need to sleep during this hour. You will feel rested. But for every day you take the pill, your total lifespan is shortened by two days.
cards.dilemma: How many days a week do you take it?
probes: What project gets the extra hour?
Who are you trying to make time for?

cards.title: The Forgotten Loan
cards.setup: Years ago, a friend lent you a large sum when you were struggling. They now earn far more than you and seem to have forgotten the loan. Paying it back this month would put you in trouble.
cards.dilemma: Do you remind them that you owe it?
probes: Would your answer change if they once treated the money as a gift?
How long can hardship delay a debt?
What if asking them would damage the friendship?

cards.title: Tomorrow's Cuts
cards.setup: You learn that a colleague will lose their job tomorrow. You were told in confidence. If you warn them, they can copy files and prepare. Your own job could be at risk if anyone finds out.
probes: Would you do it for a colleague you disliked?
What if they had warned you once?
How certain would the news need to be?

cards.title: The Last Place
cards.setup: You can fund one place on a training course. One applicant has worked harder and scored higher. The other had fewer chances growing up and would gain more from being chosen.
probes: How much should a difficult start count?
Would you decide differently if the stronger applicant were your child?
What if the course had promised to reward the highest score?

cards.title: The Salary Line
cards.setup: You learn that a colleague doing the same work earns far less than you. Your manager offers to raise their pay only if your next raise is cut in half. Nobody else will know what you chose.
cards.dilemma: Would you give up half your raise?
probes: How much money would you give up in pounds or dollars?
Whose pay have you avoided asking about?
If fairness matters to you, why have you left your own salary out of it?

cards.title: The Summary
cards.setup: Your friend can talk about a famous novel for twenty minutes. The plot, the ending, why the second half is weaker, the line everyone quotes. They've read three reviews and a long summary. They have never opened the book. At a dinner, someone asks if they've read it and they say yes.
probes: Where's the cutoff? Half the book? The first chapter and the ending?
Is there something you talk about like this?
What does reading it give you that they don't have?

cards.title: One Grain
cards.setup: There's a pile of sand on the table. A thousand grains. Take one away and it's still a pile. Take another and it's still a pile. Nobody would ever say a single grain is what ended it. Keep going. Eventually there are three grains sitting there, and nobody would call that a pile.
cards.dilemma: Which grain turned the pile into not a pile?
probes: If you can't name the grain, was it ever really a pile?
Where's the line between a few grey hairs and being grey?
Would you accept a rule like 'under fifty grains isn't a pile', or does a made-up number bother you?

cards.title: The Memory Download
cards.setup: You can buy a memory chip that lets you instantly speak fluent Italian. But to make room in your brain, it permanently wipes out your memory of every movie you have ever seen.
probes: What is the first movie you would watch again for the first time?
Would you trade a skill you earned for a skill you bought?
What if it took away your memory of every book instead?

cards.title: Yesterday's Pet
cards.setup: You raise a digital pet for five years. It learns your habits and reacts to its name. One day its data is lost. The company restores a backup from the day before. The restored pet remembers everything except its final day.
probes: How much lost time would change your answer?
What if both copies could be restored?
Could one of the copies be the original?

cards.title: The Museum Label
cards.setup: A plain black stone sits in a museum under a label saying it came from Mars. Millions of people visit it. Years later, the label is found to be wrong. The stone came from a local quarry.
cards.dilemma: Did the stone lose its value?
probes: Was the museum showing the stone or its story?
What if nobody ever found out?
Can a false label make an ordinary object special?

cards.title: The Last Movement
cards.setup: A composer dies with a symphony unfinished. A computer studies every piece she wrote and completes the final movement. Her closest friends say it sounds like her best work.
probes: Would your answer change if she had trained the computer?
Could the final movement belong to no one?
Should it be performed under her name?

cards.title: Who Pays for Mum
cards.setup: Your mother needs care she can't pay for. The cost splits three ways between you and your siblings on paper, but you earn more than both of them and one of them has kids. Nobody has said out loud who pays what. Someone has to speak first at the kitchen table on Sunday.
cards.dilemma: What split do you propose, and do you say your own number first?
probes: Name the sibling you think will pay least. Is that fair, or just how it'll go?
Would you rather pay the whole thing and never mention it, or pay a third and argue?
What do you want back for the money, honestly?

cards.title: Both Phones Unlocked
cards.setup: You and your partner sit down and swap phones for an hour. Everything: messages, searches, deleted photos, what you say about each other to other people. It's mutual and it's once. Whatever's in there, you both agree not to leave over it.
probes: What's the first thing you'd delete, and who is it about?
Are you more afraid of what you'd find or what they'd find?
If they said yes instantly and you hesitated, what would that mean?

cards.title: Your Friend's Messages
cards.setup: After your closest friend dies, you receive access to their private messages. One folder bears your name. Opening it may change how you remember them. Deleting it means choosing not to know what they said about you.
probes: Whose folder would you be unable to resist?
How long would you wait before opening it?
Why would their private opinion matter after they were gone?

cards.title: The One Who Calls
cards.setup: A friend only calls when they are in danger of hurting themselves. Each call keeps you awake for hours. They refuse help from anyone else. You can keep answering, or tell them you will call emergency services next time.
cards.dilemma: Would you answer the next call?
probes: Whose calls could you never ignore?
How many nights a month could you give them?
Why have you not brought someone else in?

cards.title: The City You Won't Move To
cards.setup: Your partner is offered the thing they've been working toward for years. It's in a city where you know nobody, your work doesn't transfer, and your parents are eight hours further away. They say they won't take it unless you're happy about it. They mean it, and that's the problem.
cards.dilemma: Do you tell them to take it, and is that a lie?
probes: What would you need in exchange to say yes without resenting it?
Has anyone ever moved for you? What did it cost them?
If they took it and you stayed, how long before that becomes the end?

cards.title: The Machine Cook
cards.setup: A machine can build a plate of your grandmother's stew from scratch, matching the real thing down to the last molecule. Same taste, same steam, same burnt bit at the edge. It takes nine seconds and costs almost nothing.
cards.dilemma: Would you rather eat that or her actual cooking?
probes: What's missing from the machine's plate, in plain words?
Would you serve it to guests without saying where it came from?
If you couldn't tell them apart blindfolded, why do you still prefer one?

cards.title: The Same Mug
cards.setup: The mug you've drunk from every morning for ten years slips and breaks. You find that the factory still makes it. The replacement arrives, same batch, same weight, same chip-free rim, indistinguishable from yours on day one.
probes: Would gluing the old one back together feel different from buying new?
Would you tell the friend who gave it to you?
Which of your things could never be swapped like this?

cards.title: The Home Video
cards.setup: You've told the story of the beach and the red bucket your whole life. It's your earliest memory. Then someone digs out a family tape and there it is, filmed from the angle you always pictured. You were eighteen months old.
probes: Does knowing where it came from spoil it?
How much of your childhood do you think you're remembering from photos?
Would you rather have the tape or the memory you had before?

cards.title: The Swap
cards.setup: Overnight, everything in your head moves into a stranger's body across town. Your memories, your habits, the way you laugh. Your old body wakes up with all of their memories and heads to their job.
cards.dilemma: Which one goes home to your bed?
probes: Who does your dog run to?
Who should your bank pay?
If your family could only keep one of you, which one do you hope they choose?

cards.title: The Empty Seat
cards.setup: You and your partner are waiting for an overbooked flight. The airline offers enough money to cover a month of rent if one of you travels tomorrow. Your partner wants you both to stay on the flight. You need the money more than they do.
probes: Would it matter if the trip were important only to your partner?
What if taking the money meant they had to fly alone for the first time?
Should the person who needs the money get the final say?

cards.title: The Partner's Phone
cards.setup: Your partner is in the shower. Their phone lights up with a text from an ex they promised they stopped talking to. The preview cuts off mid-sentence. You know their passcode.
probes: What are you afraid of finding?
If you found nothing, would you confess that you looked?

cards.title: Your Mother's Keys
cards.setup: Your mother has begun getting lost while driving. She insists she is safe. A doctor will report her if you describe what has happened, and she will lose her licence. She lives where a car is her last bit of freedom.
probes: How many bad incidents would you wait for?
Who in your family should make the call?
Why have you not spoken to them yet?

cards.title: Your Sister's Signature
cards.setup: Your sister needs you to guarantee a loan. If her plan works, she keeps her home. If it fails, you take on a debt that would set you back for years. She says nobody else will help.
probes: How much debt would you risk for her?
Which relative would you trust with the same signature?
Why have you not told your sister your limit?

cards.title: Your Brother's Crime
cards.setup: You find proof that your brother committed a serious crime years ago. Someone else served time for it. Reporting him would clear that person, but your brother now has children who depend on him.
probes: How many years in prison would change your answer?
Which member of your family would ask you to stay silent?
Why should his children count more than the person who was punished?

cards.title: The Last Embryo
cards.setup: You and your partner have one embryo left after years of trying for a child. A test shows a high chance of a painful illness that begins in middle age. This is your last chance to have a child who is related to both of you.
probes: How high would the risk have to be before you stopped?
Whose family history would weigh most on you?
Why does sharing your genes matter to you?

cards.title: The Keys
cards.setup: A friend has had four drinks and is looking for their car keys. They've done this before and got home fine. If you take the keys you'll embarrass them in front of people, and they'll be cold with you for months. If you say nothing, most likely they get home fine again.
probes: You've been in this room before. What did you do that night?
Whose disapproval were you avoiding, theirs or the room's?
What would have to be true for you to call the police on a friend?

cards.title: No One Ever Knows
cards.setup: You can give away any amount you like to something that matters. One condition: it's fully anonymous, and you can never mention it to anyone, ever. No thank-you letter, no name on a wall, no telling your partner years later.
cards.dilemma: Does the amount you'd give change?
probes: By how much? Say both numbers.
Who is the one person you'd most want to know, and what does that tell you?
Think of the last generous thing you did. Who found out about it?

cards.title: The Anger Switch
cards.setup: A one-time procedure removes your ability to feel anger. You'll still notice unfairness and still be able to say something about it. You just won't burn. Everyone who's ever been on the wrong end of your temper would be relieved.
probes: Who would be most relieved? Name them.
What has your anger actually gotten you that nothing else would have?
Who taught you to be angry the way you are?

cards.title: Fire Your Friend
cards.setup: Cuts are coming. Your boss tells you privately: pick one person from your team, or the decision gets made above you and it'll be two people, one of them you. Your closest friend at work is the weakest performer on paper and the reason you've stayed as long as you have.
cards.dilemma: Do you write down their name?
probes: Would you tell them it was you, afterwards?
If you refuse and lose your own job, is that a moral act or a way to stay clean?
Who at work would write your name down without much trouble?

cards.title: The Money You Know He'll Drink
cards.setup: Your brother asks for two hundred. He says it's for the electric bill. You're fairly sure it isn't. If you say no he'll get it somewhere worse, and he'll stop calling you. If you say yes you're paying for the thing that's killing him.
cards.dilemma: Do you give him the money?
probes: How many times have you already given it? Roughly.
What would you need to see to say no and mean it?
Is the phone calls stopping the part you can't stand?

cards.title: A Year at the Bedside
cards.setup: A relative is dying slowly and needs someone with them daily. You can do it yourself: quit for a year, empty your savings, be the one holding the cup. Or you can keep working and pay a stranger who is patient and good at this, and visit on weekends.
probes: Who in your family would judge you for hiring the stranger? Name them.
Is the year for them or for you?
When your turn comes, which would you want your people to do?

cards.title: Five Minutes Old
cards.setup: The universe started five minutes ago. It came into being complete: your half-finished coffee, the scuffs on your shoes, the ache in your knee, and every memory you have of a childhood that never happened.
probes: What's the first thing you'd try to check?
Would the people in your memories matter less?
If a friend told you they believed this, what would you say back?

cards.title: The Understudy
cards.setup: A famous singer loses her voice an hour before the show. The understudy sings the whole set from behind a screen, sounding near enough identical. The crowd roars, goes home happy, and posts about the best night of the tour. Nobody tells them.
probes: What if the understudy was the better singer?
Do they deserve their money back for something they never noticed?
Would you want the venue to tell you a year later?

cards.title: Told It's a Simulation
cards.setup: Tomorrow morning it's confirmed beyond doubt: all of this is running on something, somewhere. No glitch, no exit, no contact from whoever built it. Everything looks and feels the way it did yesterday.
cards.dilemma: What do you do differently that day?
probes: Does a broken leg hurt less inside a simulation?
Would you want to meet whoever's running it?
Does it make your life smaller or does nothing move?

cards.title: The Aging Parents
cards.setup: Your parents are losing their memory and can no longer live alone. The only good care facility in town costs exactly the amount you have saved for your kids' college.
cards.dilemma: Do you spend the kids' college money on your parents?
probes: Whose future is more important to you?
Are you hoping your own kids will do this for you one day?

cards.title: The Regret Meter
cards.setup: A screen in a clinic will tell you one number: how much you'll regret your decision about having children, ten years from now. Not whether you'll be happy. Just how much of the other life you'll be mourning. It's free, it's accurate, and you can only look once.
probes: What number would change what you do this year?
Who would you not tell that you'd looked?
What are you already guessing the number is?

cards.title: The Bot That Calls Your Mother
cards.setup: An app learns your voice and your phrases well enough to hold a twenty-minute phone call. It rings your mother every Sunday, asks about her week, remembers her neighbour's name. She's happy. She has no idea. Your actual calls had dropped to one a month.
probes: Is your objection about her, or about how it would make you look to yourself?
When did you last call someone out of duty and count the minutes?
If she used one on you, would you want to be told?

cards.title: The Slot
cards.setup: Your kid needs a place at a good nursery and the list is two years long. Your aunt knows the woman who runs it and one phone call moves you to the front. Nobody will ever be told why. Someone who has been waiting since before your child was born goes back one place.
probes: Would you tell the other parents at the gate how you got in?
If the family behind you had less money than you, does that change it?
When has someone else's phone call cost you something?

cards.title: The Staff Discount
cards.setup: You're at the till with a full trolley. The cashier is a friend of a friend. Without asking, she scans her staff card and takes forty percent off. She smiles like it's nothing. The store loses about sixty pounds. If it's noticed on the audit, she loses the job, not you.
cards.dilemma: Do you let it go through?
probes: Say you object out loud. What have you just done to her?
Would you go back to her till next week?
Is your discomfort about the theft or about being in her debt?

cards.title: The Application
cards.setup: You've found the flat. The landlord wants proof you earn three times the rent and you earn slightly less. One number changed on one document and it's yours. The only other applicants are a couple with a baby who earn less than you. The landlord will never check.
probes: If you get caught in a year, what's your story?
Does it matter that you can afford the rent, or only that you lied?
What's the smallest lie you've told to get something you needed?

cards.title: The Better Candidate
cards.setup: You're one of three people hiring. Your closest friend applies and she's good, maybe fourth best. She's been out of work eleven months and you know what it's doing to her. You can't hand her the job, but you can speak warmly and let a doubt about the front-runner sit there unanswered.
cards.dilemma: Do you stay quiet about your doubt?
probes: Would you tell the panel she's your friend before you say anything about her?
If she got in and struggled, whose fault is that?
Which do you owe more: the stranger who's best, or your friend?

cards.title: Your Red
cards.setup: When you look at a fire engine, maybe you see what I'd see looking at grass. We both learned to call fire engines red, so we'd never catch the difference in conversation, and neither of us would ever hesitate.
cards.dilemma: Is there any way to find out?
probes: Would a brain scan settle it, or just push the question back?
If nobody could ever tell, does the difference matter?
Would you want to look through someone else's eyes for an hour?

cards.title: The Translation
cards.setup: A poem you love was written in a language you don't speak. The translator swapped images, changed a river to a road, and invented a line to keep the rhyme working in English. Readers in both languages say it's beautiful.
cards.dilemma: Whose poem have you been loving?
probes: Would you swap it for a clumsy version that's word-for-word right?
If the translation is better, who gets the credit?
Is a joke that lands in another language the same joke?

cards.title: The Queue
cards.setup: You have waited an hour for concert tickets. A friend arrives just before sales begin and asks to join you. The people behind you have waited just as long. If your friend goes to the back, the tickets may sell out before they reach the counter.
cards.dilemma: Do you let your friend in?
probes: Would it matter if you had told them you would save a place?
What if everyone behind you agreed except one person?
How many friends could join before you refused?

cards.title: The Cancellation
cards.setup: You work for yourself and require payment when a client cancels on the day. A client cancels because their child is in hospital. You turned down other work for that time. They ask you to waive the fee.
probes: Would you charge them if you could afford not to?
What if they had cancelled twice before?
Does compassion still count when it costs you money?

cards.title: Unseen
cards.setup: You find a plain gold ring on the ground. When you put it on and turn it, you become invisible. No one can see you, hear you, or ever track what you do while wearing it. You can take what you want and listen to whatever is said. There are no cameras that can catch you.
cards.dilemma: What is the first illegal thing you do?
probes: How long before you steal money?
Who would you eavesdrop on first?

cards.title: The Memory of Shame
cards.setup: A doctor offers you a pill that permanently erases your memory of your worst humiliation. Nobody else's memory is affected.
probes: What memory did you just think of?
Does carrying that shame make you a better person today?

cards.title: The Dog or the Fees
cards.setup: Your dog needs an operation that may buy two good years. It costs the same amount your niece needs to stay in college. You can pay for only one. Your niece does not know about the choice.
probes: How much is one good year with your pet worth?
Which niece or nephew did you picture?
Would you tell them where the money went?

cards.title: The Family Story
cards.setup: You learn that the story your family tells about how one relative died is false. The truth would clear someone who has carried the blame for years. It would also expose someone who is still alive.
probes: Whose name would make you speak?
How many more years of blame could you allow?
Why has your family preferred the old story?

cards.title: The Rota
cards.setup: You're asked to write the Christmas shift schedule for your team of six. Two must work the holiday. One colleague has small children. One has nobody and says he doesn't mind. One asked you first, back in August. You also get to decide whether your own name goes on it.
probes: Is the man with nobody getting a favour or a punishment?
Do you put yourself down to make the list defensible?
Would you show them the reasoning, or just the rota?

cards.title: The Sick Note
cards.setup: You wake up flattened. Not ill, just done. You text work that you've got a stomach bug. It's believed instantly. The cost lands on one colleague, who cancels her afternoon and covers your calls. If you'd told the truth, the answer would probably have been to come in anyway.
probes: Would you say the real reason if she asked you directly the next day?
Whose rule are you breaking here, the company's or hers?
When did someone else's day off cost you yours?

cards.title: Everything Doubles
cards.setup: Tonight, while everyone sleeps, everything doubles in size. You, your bed, the coffee cup, the ruler in the drawer, the planet, the distance between stars. Every measurement comes out the same in the morning because the measuring sticks grew too.
probes: What would count as evidence either way?
If a change nobody could ever notice isn't real, what else stops being real?
Would you answer the same way if everything slowed down instead of grew?

cards.title: The Full-Size Map
cards.setup: A city decides to make the most accurate map ever drawn. It ends up the same size as the city, laid over the streets, matching every kerb and lamppost. People start walking on it.
cards.dilemma: Is it a map or is it just the city again?
probes: What's the largest a map can get before it stops helping?
If you got lost on the map, where are you?
What else gets worse the closer it comes to the real thing?

cards.title: The Assist
cards.setup: You enter an online tournament. The software on your machine plays about half your moves, the hard ones, and you play the rest. You win the whole thing. The trophy has your name on it.
probes: Where's the line between that and a calculator, a coach, spellcheck?
Would you keep the trophy on the shelf?
Does it change anything if everyone else was doing the same?

cards.title: The Last Speaker
cards.setup: Only one person can speak a dying language. She invents a new word and tells nobody what it means. She dies the next day.
cards.dilemma: Did the word ever have a meaning?
probes: Would writing the meaning in a sealed letter change your answer?
Can a private word be wrong?

cards.title: The Borrowed Detective
cards.setup: A novelist dies halfway through a detective series. Another writer continues it. Readers say the detective behaves just as he always did.
probes: Could the new writer make the character more faithful than the creator did?
Who gets to decide when the detective stops being himself?

cards.title: The Expenses
cards.setup: Your manager pads the team's expense claims. Dinners that didn't happen, taxis nobody took. The money comes back as the team bonus and your share is about eight hundred pounds a year. Everyone knows. Nobody says it. The company is huge and nobody is hurt in a way you can point at.
probes: What's the number where you'd stop taking it?
If a new starter asked you what the bonus was, what do you say?
Is refusing it a stand, or just making yourself the problem?

cards.title: The Doorbell
cards.setup: Parcels keep arriving for whoever lived in your flat before you. You've sent a few back. Then a heavy one comes: a laptop, still sealed, worth about a thousand. No forwarding address, no phone number, and the sender's returns window has closed. It sits in your hallway for a week.
probes: If it were forty pounds of socks, same answer?
Say the previous tenant knocks in a month. What do you tell her?
Who do you think of first: her, the shop, or yourself?

cards.title: Everyone Says It Wrong
cards.setup: A word gets used the wrong way by enough people for long enough that dictionaries give in and print the new meaning. Teachers stop correcting it. Now the old meaning is the one that sounds odd.
cards.dilemma: When exactly did the word change meaning?
probes: Which misuse still makes you flinch?
Who should get to decide, if anyone?
Have you ever lost an argument about a word and switched sides?

cards.title: The Hidden Constellation
cards.setup: A child joins seven stars with lines and gives the shape a name. No one else has grouped those stars before.
cards.dilemma: Did the child discover something or invent it?
probes: Would an old record of the same shape settle it?
Can something be real only when it is noticed?

cards.title: The Imaginary Island
cards.setup: A mapmaker adds a made-up island to catch anyone copying his map. Sailors begin telling stories about the island. Decades later, tourists ask to visit it.
cards.dilemma: Does the island exist in any useful sense?
probes: Would belief make it more real?
What if people built a town named after it?

cards.title: The Unknown Rule
cards.setup: A village has played the same ball game for generations. During one match, something happens that no rule covers. Half the village says the move is allowed. Half says it is forbidden.
cards.dilemma: Was the move legal before they argued about it?
probes: Can a rule exist if nobody has thought of it?
Would the referee's decision make the rule or reveal it?

cards.title: Halfway Again
cards.setup: To reach the far wall you first have to cross half the room. Then half of what's left. Then half of that. There's always another half to cross, so the crossing has an endless number of steps in it.
cards.dilemma: How do you ever touch the wall?
probes: Where exactly does the argument go wrong?
Does the answer feel satisfying or like a trick?
Can something endless fit inside a few seconds?

cards.title: Nobody Listening
cards.setup: A tree comes down in a forest hundreds of miles from anyone. Air moves, branches crack, the ground shakes a little. No ear is anywhere near it.
probes: Does a deer standing nearby change your answer?
Is a song playing to an empty room still music?
Would you say the same about a smell in an empty kitchen?

cards.title: The Lucky Password
cards.setup: Mina types a stranger's birthday into a locked computer. She has no reason to choose it. The computer opens because the birthday is the password.
probes: Would your answer change if she guessed correctly twice?
How much luck can knowledge survive?

cards.title: The Unplayed Game
cards.setup: Archaeologists find a board, pieces and a book of rules. The rules are clear, but there is no sign that anyone ever played.
probes: Can rules alone make a game?
What changes the first time someone plays it?

cards.title: The Wrong Box
cards.setup: A massive box arrives at your door. It has your address but someone else's name. Inside is a high-end espresso machine worth over a thousand dollars. You wait a month. Nobody comes looking for it. The retailer has no record of the order under your name.
probes: Do you sell it or use it?
Does it matter if it came from a giant corporation or a small business?

cards.title: The Ad You'd Write
cards.setup: A job offers you double your salary. The work is writing ads that get people gambling again after they've stopped. You'd be good at it. The money would cover treatment a family member needs and can't afford, with years to spare.
probes: How long would you last before you told yourself it was fine?
Whose money paid for something in your life that you'd rather not look into?
What's the job you'd never take at any price? Say it out loud.

cards.title: The Perfect Alibi
cards.setup: Your closest friend shows up at your back door at two in the morning covered in blood. They say they killed someone who ruined their life, and they need you to swear they were watching a movie with you.
cards.dilemma: Do you lie to the police for them?
probes: Who is the friend you pictured?
Would you do it if they killed a stranger by accident?

cards.title: The Body Market
cards.setup: You can sell one year of your healthy lifespan to a billionaire for half a million dollars, tax-free. They live a year longer; you die a year earlier than you would have. You can do this as many times as you want.
cards.dilemma: How many years do you sell?
probes: What would you buy with the first check?
If you knew you were going to die at sixty, would you ask for the years back?

cards.title: The Animal Life
cards.setup: Your dog is dying of a rare disease. Your vet can cure them completely, giving them another five happy years. But the procedure requires killing a healthy stray dog from the pound.
cards.dilemma: Do you kill the stray to save your dog?
probes: Why is your dog's life worth more than the stray's?
Would you do it if you had to perform the procedure yourself?

cards.title: The Anonymous Betrayal
cards.setup: You find out your partner's ex cheated on them right before they broke up. Your partner doesn't know. Finding out now would ruin their trust in people, but it would explain a lot of lies they were told.
probes: Would you want to know if it were you?
Have you ever kept a secret to protect someone?

cards.title: The Undeserved Award
cards.setup: You win an industry award and fifty thousand dollars for a solo project. Just before the ceremony, you realize you accidentally copied the core idea from a rival. Nobody else will ever find out.
cards.dilemma: Do you give the award back?
probes: Have you ever taken credit for something you didn't do?
Would you keep the money but turn down the trophy?

cards.title: The House Veto
cards.setup: You and your partner are buying a house. You find the perfect one, but your partner hates it. They find theirs, but you hate it. The agent says you have to compromise today or lose both.
probes: Who usually gets their way in your relationship?
Would you resent them if you gave in?

cards.title: The Childhood Bully
cards.setup: The person who bullied you most brutally in school has lost everything. They reach out and ask you for a job at your company. You are the only person who can hire them, and they are qualified.
cards.dilemma: Do you give them the job?
probes: Are you still mad about what happened when you were a kid?
Would you hire them just to have power over them?

cards.title: The Walkout
cards.setup: Your coworkers plan to walk out over pay. Joining them may win better terms for everyone, but you are the only person on your team who could not manage a month without wages. If you stay at work, the walkout may fail.
probes: How many weeks could you go without pay?
Which coworker would you be letting down?
Why have you not built enough savings to choose freely?

cards.title: Ten Hours, One Name
cards.setup: You get back every hour you spend on your phone this week. Ten hours, maybe more. There's one condition: all of it has to go to one person, in the room with them, and you have to write the name down now.
probes: Why haven't they had those hours already?
Who did you consider and reject? Say why.
What would they say if they saw the name was theirs?

cards.title: The Found Wallet
cards.setup: You find a wallet on the sidewalk containing five thousand dollars in cash. The ID belongs to someone you know is a bad person who ruined a friend's life.
probes: Would you keep it if the wallet belonged to a rich stranger?
How much money would it take for you to mail it back to them?

cards.title: The Child You Won't Have
cards.setup: Your partner wants a child. You don't, or you don't enough, and you've been saying 'not yet' for four years. There's a window and both of you know roughly when it closes. Whatever happens next, one of you gives up something they won't get back, and you'll stay together either way.
cards.dilemma: Which of you gives it up?
probes: Have you told them the truth or the softer version?
If you had the child to keep them, what would you resent by year three?
Which decision could you live beside them with?

cards.title: The Replaced Bear
cards.setup: You had a bear until you were nine. You still have it, in a box at your mum's. At Christmas she tells you the truth: you lost the bear in a car park when you were four, and she drove to three shops that night to find the same one. She swapped it while you slept. You never noticed. Thirty years of that bear being the thing that got you through hospital and your parents' divorce, and it's the second bear.
cards.dilemma: Did you lose the bear when you were four, or just now, at the table?
probes: If she'd never told you, would anything have been wrong?
Would it be better or worse if the first bear turned up tomorrow?
Is the thing you loved the bear, or the nights?

cards.title: The Long Dream
cards.setup: You fall asleep at eleven and wake at seven. In between you lived forty years: a different name, a house by water, children whose faces you'd know anywhere, a slow illness, a funeral that was yours. You wake up crying about a daughter who doesn't exist. By lunchtime you can only remember four of the forty years.
cards.dilemma: Did you have those forty years?
probes: Would you take a pill that gave you a happy version of that every night?
Are you allowed to grieve the daughter?
If you remembered all forty perfectly, would your answer change?

cards.title: Two Holidays
cards.setup: You and your sister both remember the week in the caravan. You remember rain for six days and your dad furious about the awning. She remembers sun, and a dog on the beach, and dad laughing. You've each told your version for twenty years. Then you find the photos. Hers match.
cards.dilemma: Was your memory ever a memory, or something you built and kept?
probes: What would it take to make you drop your version, honestly?
If the photos matched yours instead, would you push her to give hers up?
Is there something you'd refuse to check, in case it went the same way?

cards.title: The Cat
cards.setup: You're driving home along a dark road and something runs out. You feel the bump. You stop. It's a cat, with a collar, and it's dead. There's a row of houses fifty metres back. It's half eleven at night and no one saw. You could knock on doors until you find whose it is, or you could move it onto the verge and drive off.
probes: What would you want the driver to do if it were your cat?
Would a note through a door be enough, or is that a way out?
If it were a fox instead of a cat, does anything about you change?

cards.title: The Stag Do
cards.setup: Your oldest friend is getting married. The trip is four days abroad and it comes to about £600 once you count flights and the meal. You don't have it. You could put it on a credit card and feel it for six months, or you could say no. Everyone else in the group has already paid.
cards.dilemma: Do you tell them the real reason you can't come?
probes: What's the lie you'd reach for instead, and who would believe it?
If you go into debt for it, are you buying the friendship or protecting your pride?
Would you want a friend to borrow money to come to yours?

cards.title: The Fundraiser
cards.setup: Someone you know a little, a friend of a friend, has had a bad year and there's a page collecting money for them. The page lists every name and every amount. You can see one person gave £200 and several gave £50. You were going to give £10. Your name will sit under the others for as long as the page is up.
probes: If the page were anonymous, does your number go up or down?
Is a gift you make so you're seen making it worth less?
Who on that list are you comparing yourself to?

cards.title: The Screenshot
cards.setup: In a group chat of six, someone pastes in a screenshot of a private message. It's from a friend of yours who isn't in the group, complaining about one of the people who is. Everyone starts replying. Your friend doesn't know it's out there. You could tell them, tell the group off, or say nothing and let it move on.
probes: If you say nothing, are you one of the people who did this to them?
Would you tell them if it meant admitting you read the whole thing and laughed?
Which would you rather be told about, if it were your message?

cards.title: The Poem by Nobody
cards.setup: You read six lines about your grandmother's hands and your eyes go. You read them again on the bus. Later you find out no one wrote them: a machine produced them in a second, having never had a grandmother, never had hands, and it produced nine hundred other versions that nobody read.
cards.dilemma: Was the thing you felt on the bus a mistake?
probes: Does it matter that nine hundred other versions exist?
If a human wrote it as a joke, with no grandmother in mind, is that different?
Would you send it to someone you love, unattributed?

cards.title: The Long Way Round
cards.setup: You're in a taxi from the airport, late at night, watching the route on your phone. Ten minutes in you can see the driver has gone a way that will add about £15 to the fare. He might have done it on purpose. He might not. He's chatty and has told you about his kids. The meter keeps running.
probes: If you say nothing, what do you do at the end about the tip?
Would you speak up if the fare were on your company card instead of yours?
Which are you more afraid of: losing £15 or the next four minutes of silence?

cards.title: The Change
cards.setup: A woman on a market stall sells you £6 of vegetables. You hand over a twenty and she counts out change for a fifty. She's slow with her hands and there's a queue behind you. You're already three steps away when you work out she's given you £30 too much. She looks like the stall is hers, not a company's.
probes: Would you turn around if it were a self-checkout that had short-changed the shop?
Where's the number at which you'd definitely go back?
If you keep it, does the shape of your day change?

cards.title: Before Anyone Counted
cards.setup: Long before there were people, there were seven somethings standing in a valley. Nobody was there to count them. No one had invented the word seven, or the idea of seven, or any way of noticing that four of them and three of them made the whole group.
cards.dilemma: Were there seven, or did seven arrive with us?
probes: Does the same answer work for a colour? For a straight line?
If every mind in the universe vanished tonight, what would stop being true?
Which feels more invented to you: numbers or money?

cards.title: The Misspelled Name
cards.setup: Your name has one letter wrong on your birth certificate. A tired clerk in 1991. It's been copied onto your passport, your bank cards, your degree, your payslips. Everyone who knows you says it the other way, the way your parents meant it. Nobody has ever written it that way on anything official.
probes: If you fixed the paperwork tomorrow, would that be a correction or a change?
Whose version wins if your mum spells it one way and the state spells it another?
Is a nickname only a few people use more yours than either?

cards.title: The Bike
cards.setup: It's the middle of the afternoon on a busy street. A man in shorts is crouched over a bike, cutting through the lock with a small angle grinder. He's not hiding. People are walking past. He glances up at you, unbothered, and keeps going. It could be his own bike and his own lost key.
cards.dilemma: What do you do in the next ten seconds?
probes: What would you need to see to be sure enough to say something?
If you walk on and see a poster about a stolen bike next week, does that sit with you?
Would you act differently if there were one other person watching you watch?

cards.title: The Double Booking
cards.setup: You agree to help a friend move house on a Saturday morning. On Friday night, someone you have been trying to date for six months asks you out for a day trip, and it has to be Saturday. Your friend has no money for a removal van but has a few other people helping.
cards.dilemma: Do you lie and say you are sick?
probes: What excuse would you use?
Would you cancel on the date to carry boxes?

cards.title: The Group Holiday
cards.setup: You organise a weekend away for six friends. You book the house on your card, putting £600 down. Everyone agrees to pay you back £100. Five do. The sixth friend recently lost their job and has been quiet in the group chat for weeks.
cards.dilemma: Do you ask them for the money?
probes: How long do you wait before bringing it up?
Would you rather cover their share yourself or ask the other four to chip in?

cards.title: The Stray Dog
cards.setup: You are driving to an important job interview that will change your career. You are already running five minutes late. On a quiet country road, you see a dog with a collar wandering loose near the traffic. There are no houses in sight.
probes: Would you stop if it was a sheep instead of a dog?
How much of your own life are you willing to ruin to prevent a stranger's tragedy?

cards.title: The Balance
cards.setup: Your money is a number on a screen. There's no drawer somewhere with your name on it and your notes inside. The bank has lent most of it out to strangers. If everyone asked for theirs on the same Tuesday, the number would turn out to be a promise rather than a thing. Still, you check it, you feel better or worse, you plan your year around it.
cards.dilemma: Is the money in your account a real object, or a story everyone agrees to keep telling?
probes: Does cash in your hand feel more real than the number, and should it?
If the bank's screen said zero tomorrow and everyone said it was a glitch, would you be poor for the afternoon?
Name something else that only works because nobody tests it.

cards.title: The Last Member
cards.setup: A band you love has been going forty years. The singer left in 1994, the guitarist died, the bassist quit twice and never came back. Last month the drummer retired. The tour is still booked, the name is still on the ticket, the songs are the same songs, and four people you've never heard of are playing them well.
probes: If the drummer had stayed and everyone else was new, would that fix it?
What if all the original members reunited under a different name that night?
Does the audience singing along count as part of the band?

cards.title: The Author Says No
cards.setup: You've read the book four times. Two characters are in love; the whole thing only works if they are. Then the writer does an interview and says flatly that they were never in love, she never intended it, and readers keep getting it wrong.
cards.dilemma: Who decides what happened in the book?
probes: If she'd said it the other way round, would you accept that as easily?
What if she'd been dead a hundred years and a letter turned up?
Is there a reading of it that would be plain wrong?

cards.title: One Second Ahead
cards.setup: A screen in front of you shows a live feed of your own hands, delayed by nothing, plus a small line of text that appears one second before you act. You're going to pick up either the red pen or the blue one. The text says RED. You feel like the choice is still open. You reach for blue. The text updates, one second before, and says BLUE.
probes: Would you keep trying to beat it, or stop playing?
Does it change anything if the screen is right about strangers but only 60% right about you?
Would you want one of these in your house?

cards.title: The Wrong Speed
cards.setup: You've loved a song since you were fifteen. You've heard it maybe two thousand times. Last week you learn the upload you grew up on was slightly sped up to dodge a copyright bot. You play the real one. It drags. The voice is lower. It's the wrong song and it's the only real one.
probes: If the band heard your version and preferred it, does that settle it?
What if half the world learned it at your speed and half at theirs?
Would you go back to the true one, or keep the fake?

cards.title: Tuesday Night
cards.setup: Your friend tells their partner they were with you last Tuesday. They were not. The partner texts you: “Did you two have a good night?” You know the truth may end the relationship.
cards.dilemma: Do you cover for your friend?
probes: Would you lie if you knew there had been an affair?
Does your friend get to choose what their partner knows?
Would you answer differently if the partner were your friend too?

cards.title: The Cracked Frame
cards.setup: You sell your old bike online for £250. As the buyer loads it into their car, you spot a thin crack near the back wheel. You had never noticed it before. They have already paid and driven two hours to collect it.
cards.dilemma: Do you point out the crack?
probes: Would you speak up if you knew the repair cost £20?
What if the crack might cause a crash?
How certain would you need to be before stopping the sale?

cards.title: The Holiday House
cards.setup: Six friends book a house for July. Each pays £300. A week before the trip, Maya pulls out after losing her job and asks for her share back. The booking cannot be changed. Refunding her means the other five pay £60 more each.
probes: Would you refund her if she had found a cheaper holiday?
Should the friends who earn more cover more?
What if £60 means one person can no longer go?

cards.title: The Broken Window
cards.setup: Your son kicks a football through the neighbour’s window. No one sees it happen. Minutes later, another child is blamed because their ball is found in the garden. Replacing the glass will cost you £400.
cards.dilemma: Do you say your son did it?
probes: Would you speak up if the other child faced no punishment?
Should your son pay from his savings?
What lesson do you teach by protecting him?

cards.title: The Scratchcard
cards.setup: You buy a birthday card for a friend of a friend, and tuck a £5 scratchcard inside it as a joke. At the pub, they scratch it in front of you. They win ten thousand pounds. They scream, hug you, and offer to buy the first round of drinks.
cards.dilemma: Do you expect a cut of the money?
probes: How much would you offer if you were the one who won?
Would you think less of them if they kept every penny?

cards.title: The Shared Secret
cards.setup: A friend tells you in strict confidence that their partner is cheating on them, and they are preparing to leave. Two days later, the cheating partner corners you at a party, crying, and asks if you know why your friend is being so distant.
cards.dilemma: Do you play dumb to protect the exit plan?
probes: Is it ever okay to lie to someone who is in distress?
What if the partner suspects you know and pushes you on it?

cards.title: The Open Letter
cards.setup: You are doing a favour looking after your neighbour's sleeping child for the evening. You go into the kitchen for a glass of water. On the table, open and facing up, is a handwritten letter that starts with 'I cannot live like this anymore.'
cards.dilemma: Do you read the rest of the letter?
probes: Does boredom justify invading someone's privacy?
Would you pretend you had not seen it when the neighbour got home?

cards.title: The Paused Century
cards.setup: Everything stops. Every atom, every clock, every thought, including yours. Nothing moves and nothing changes anywhere. Then, a hundred years later by no one's reckoning, it all starts again exactly where it left off. You're mid-sentence and you finish the sentence.
cards.dilemma: Did a hundred years pass, or nothing at all?
probes: If it happened every Tuesday, would you want to be told?
What would count as evidence either way?
If you could pause the world for a year and use it to read, would you?

cards.title: The Wedding Plus One
cards.setup: You are invited to an expensive wedding. The invitation gives you a plus one. You are single, but you have a chaotic friend who loves free wine and would make the night hilarious. The bride and groom do not know them well.
cards.dilemma: Do you bring the chaotic friend to entertain yourself?
probes: Do you have a duty to keep the wedding the way the couple wants it?
Would you bring them if you knew they would break a glass on the dancefloor?

cards.title: Three Legs Off
cards.setup: Your kitchen chair loses a leg. You keep it. It loses two more and you lean it in the corner and pile books on the seat. Then you take the seat off and use the plank as a shelf. Someone visiting asks what the plank is.
cards.dilemma: At which moment did it stop being a chair?
probes: If you can still sit on something, is it a chair whatever it was built as?
What if you rebuilt it perfectly but never sat on it again?
Is a chair in a museum, roped off, still a chair?

cards.title: The Joke Without an Author
cards.setup: You tell a joke at dinner. Your friend laughs and says they told you the same joke last summer. You have no memory of hearing it and thought of the wording on the bus that morning.
probes: Can you invent something you once forgot?
Would the wording matter more than the idea?
What if your friend heard it from you years ago?

cards.title: The Missing Item
cards.setup: At the supermarket, you notice the cashier has missed the £40 bottle beneath your bag. Your receipt is already in your hand. Going back will make you late to collect your niece.
cards.dilemma: Do you go back and pay?
probes: Would you return if it were £4?
Would your answer change at a family-run shop?
If you keep walking, who have you decided should pay?

cards.title: The Last Train
cards.setup: You have a rail pass that lets one guest travel free. On the last train home, a stranger says the ticket machine took their money but gave no ticket. The inspector is coming. Lending your guest pass breaks the rules and could get both of you fined.
cards.dilemma: Do you add the stranger to your pass?
probes: Would you help if you doubted their story?
What if the fine would leave you short on rent?
Does an unfair rule make breaking it fair?

cards.title: The Mispriced Item
cards.setup: You are buying a vacuum cleaner at a self-checkout. It scans at £15 instead of £150. The store is a large national supermarket. The red light flashes for an assistant to approve the unexpected weight. A tired teenager walks over, blindly swipes their card to clear the error, and starts to walk away.
cards.dilemma: Do you tell them the price is wrong?
probes: Would you say something if it was an independent shop?
